summary.name: Motion Poster. The label was normalized from a moving street-poster description. Category: Motion Design and Cinematography. Provenance is normalized.
summary.visualIdentity: Build a complete static poster first, with a clear headline, imagery, supporting information, and negative space. Motion then uses local loops, layout changes, or controlled boundary crossings while keeping useful still frames. Important text needs reading holds, and loop endpoints must match.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to announcements, UI and product storytelling, editorial and minimalist layouts, and staged geometric motion posters. Inferred from combinations: social posters, hero banners, and event or film posters. Adapt or omit it when a layout change weakens the subject's explanation.
summary.limitations: Motion must not weaken headline hierarchy or reading time. Recomposition is unsuitable when it changes hierarchy without explaining the subject, or when the anchored subject crops key details or pushes text into unsafe areas. Pinning fails when it disrupts layout or waits on live scroll input. The accent fill is decorative only, because it reaches just 3.499:1 contrast with the background for text.
summary.palette: Example tokens, used only when no approved palette is supplied: background #F4EDDF, foreground #273B44, and accent_1 #B66A4B. Foreground on background is 10.04:1, which passes normal text. Gradients are disabled. Task or brand colors override these, and assets must not be recolored. Two-color checks do not cover images, video, or animated lighting, so composited frames must be rechecked.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Animate selected elements and layout transitions from the static poster, matching start and end states. Preserve deliberate cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections, and reading holds; easing is not required everywhere. Video is driven by seekable composition time, while hover, scroll, and pointer behavior apply only to interactive delivery. The optional motion-007 pinned recomposition applies only if the scene supports its actions.
summary.audio: Unspecified. The style mandates no audio layer, tempo, genre, instrument, or voice. Suggest music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence based on topic, audience, and motion, honoring supplied requirements first. Speech must stay intelligible and must not compete with reading holds. No audio assets are supplied.
summary.assetRequirements: Required: the approved static poster inputs, including exact copy, headline, and imagery; none are supplied here. Fonts and local assets must load before rendering. Raster crops need Cropper.js recipes that preserve headline clearance and source identity. Optional: tldraw exports for editable artwork, or mo.js effects with pre-resolved random values. Asset permissions are unspecified.
summary.combinations: Standalone use suits announcements. Suggested hybrids, inferred from the catalog: style-051 spot-color screen-print layers (navy, rust, cream paper; no gradients) for event and film posters, and style-101 restrained image-area parallax with static text for social posters and hero banners. Still frames must remain useful, and the headline must not receive parallax.
summary.productionApproach: Build the static poster first. HTML/CSS and SVG are the style renderers. A paused GSAP timeline is the primary motion engine, while Motion, mo.js, or Anime.js are optional, each with one owner per property. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for timing, sync, validation, and export. Remotion is used only under its documented fallback condition, with the reason recorded. Verify seeks, decoded frames, and loop seams.
